title: RISE Live: interactive scenes
acceptance: The sandbox learns to listen and is not opened (design §1 item 5): the reader's pointer and keys go into a generated scene's worker as rise.input (scene/input), built by RISE from the event's own numbers ({ type, x, y, buttons, key, modifiers }, x and y in the canvas's CSS pixels), never a DOM node, element reference or event object, at most 120 pointer inputs a second (moves coalesced, presses and releases never dropped) and 30 keys a second.

Only a scene that declares it listens (export const listens or rise.listen at init) is given input; a scene that does not is given nothing, its canvas stays inert and hidden, and it behaves exactly as before (no scene/input in the worker's message log).

Keys reach a scene only while its canvas has the focus, which only the reader gives it, with a visible ring; never the instrument's keys (Space, R, F, minus, equals, brackets, Escape): Space still pauses from a focused scene, the arrows go to it, and Escape returns the focus to the stage.

What the reader set comes out as scene.input { scene, control, value } via rise.emit: control [a-z0-9-]{1,40}, value a finite number, a boolean or a string of at most 80 characters, 10 a second per control with the trailing value kept, at most 64 controls a scene, taken only while the scene handles the reader's input; anything else is dropped with a scene.input.refused note, and a scene emitting junk never stalls the reading.
The runtime journals scene.input; perception carries it with the reader's next words in words of action; nothing goes up on a timer; the card journals it and has no perception.

A tested widget set in rise.lib (design §6): slider, a draggable point in a frame's coordinates, a step-through; each draws in the style's defaults, hit-tests the delivered inputs, keeps and exposes .value, emits on change, and takes a focused scene's arrows; rise.lib.focusable orders several. Not a second format.
Touch is held (touch-action: none) only over the widgets' hit regions, never a dead zone for scrolling the chat around a card; the words' band keeps its own drag over a scene.
Accessibility: every scene.input is announced in the stage's hidden live region, and the widgets' labels and values are mirrored in a hidden list (aria-live off).
The guide teaches Live's model rise.listen, the widget set, rise.emit, that the reader's moves come back as perception, and the restraint; the card's tool text and the Worker are unchanged.

The demonstration (VISION §2.5's neural-network page): a generated scene of a two-weight network with sliders for the weights, a draggable input point and the output drawn live, written as a mock-beats reading that invites the reader to move it; venue e2e holds the round trip from a move to the journal to the perception line, the keys, the band, the inert undeclared scene and the junk scene; the card's e2e passes with the non-interactive fixtures unchanged.
